english.title: Daytime trespass in pursuit of game - poaching
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) during the daytime trespassed by entering or being upon land at **(..SPECIFY PLACE..) in search or pursuit of game, woodcocks, snipes or conies
english.legislation: Contrary to section 30 of the Game Act 1831.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The penalty for this offence was increased from 1st August 2022, for offences committed on or after that date see H100776.
(ii) See also the associated offence wording as follows: H2499 for trespass by five or more persons.
(iii) See section 4A of the Game Law (Amendment) Act 1960 for forfeiture of vehicles.
(iv) Despite being a non-imprisonable offence, this offence is recordable, see regulation 3 of, and the Schedule to, the National Police Records (Recordable Offences) Regulations 2000.
(v) See the prosecution time limit in section 41 of the Game Act 1831 - prosecution for this offence should be commenced within three calendar months after the commission of the offence.
